Class WindowHandle

java.lang.Object
com.trevlar.slotkit.api.window.WindowHandle
Direct Known Subclasses:
SlotHandle
public abstract sealed class WindowHandle extends Object permits SlotHandle
The base of the window's typed handles: an immutable value that addresses one thing by its Address, never by a live reference. The menu and every Slot are recreated on each reopen, so a held reference would go stale. equals and hashCode are over the address and the mode scope, so two handles naming the same thing in the same scope are interchangeable and safe as map keys.

Two layers

  • Generic (here, for every kind): set(BehaviorKey, Decl) and behavior(BehaviorKey) reach any behavior, including ones added later, with no new handle code.
  • Named methods (the typed subclass): SlotHandle.gate(...), thin wrappers over the generic layer.

The handle never returns the raw backing (no getSlot()). Reads go through behavior(BehaviorKey), which resolves the cascade and is never null. Writes go to WindowEngine.set(ModeScope, Address, BehaviorKey, Decl).

Sealed to the one kind it serves, slots; a new kind would add a subclass. A handle is resolved on each call, so one consumer line addresses the same thing across reopens, across sides, and for vanilla and created slots alike.
